notes: Checkpoint acceptance ledger: design crash rows, §11.2 cases and C3–C5b-2 review findings and C6b VM findings; the integration test pins IDs and coverage structure. Full-suite build.sh test runs check fully qualified references against the compiled registry and ignored status, not semantic sufficiency.

C6b replaced every planned VM slot with VM scenario names (crash matrix, hostile set, client fixtures); the remaining gaps are kiln-side cases, the Firecracker half of legacy behavior and two recorded LOWs. Unrated nonblocking observations are LOW, except the moderate VM coverage observation (MEDIUM); original reported severities are otherwise retained.

cases.vm_note: A recorded LOW, declared, not fixed: kiln refuses /proc/x and /sys/fs/cgroup/x only after kilnd has admitted the create, with no backend ID reported, so kilnd keeps each row FAILED with its reservation charged (an ambiguous reservation) and Delete refuses it. Production does not declare these rows; the VM scenario requires exactly one such row per refused create, the one the error names, and declares it for its end-of-scenario check. /dev/shm/x is created and its capture refused.

cases.gap: kiln (repository kiln, crate kiln, commit 8735907): checkpoint::manifest::tests::hostile_structure_is_refused points a hardlink entry at itself, at an earlier directory and at a later symlink; a hardlink must name an earlier file entry, so no cycle can be encoded. cases.vm_note: A sandbox whose shim dies out of band keeps its row and charge, and kilnd's strict removal cannot prove the backend gone, since its probe of the dead PID 1 fails. When kiln lists exactly that run once as stale, Delete collects it by ID and proves it absent. The VM scenario kills the shim, waits for kiln to list the run stale, then requires one Delete to answer DELETED, release the reservation and leave no run, with no root kiln gc (on the Mac: kilnd::manager::tests::delete_collects_a_backend_listed_stale_and_releases_it and kilnd::manager::tests::delete_never_collects_a_backend_listed_running).

findings.summary: Removal could delete another generation and certify absence for the wrong generation.
Removal waited behind a full cleanup lane after changing artifact state.
A remover could delete a replacement generation after checking a stale inode.
findings.gap: Replacement-inode race regression belongs to kiln; no direct kilnd-tree test drives the pathname-rebinding interleaving. Stays with kiln's own tests: no kilnd VM scenario drives kiln's internal interleavings.

findings.summary: Unchecked removal stopped sweeping malformed staging/removing names.
findings.gap: Malformed-name unchecked-removal regression belongs to kiln and is not checked by this ledger test. Stays with kiln's own tests: no kilnd VM scenario drives kiln's internal interleavings.

findings.summary: Cleanup permit was released immediately before state settlement.
findings.gap: The lane test covers immediate refusal, but no direct regression observes permit retention through settlement; a test hook is needed.

findings.summary: A busy stale-generation removal could retain a tombstone that blocks the real generation.
The universal directory-lock safety description overstated staging-failure cleanup.
findings.gap: Kiln staging failure cleanup can unlink its unique name without its lock; no kilnd-tree regression or documentation guard pins the narrowed invariant. Stays with kiln's own tests: no kilnd VM scenario drives kiln's internal interleavings.

findings.summary: The stale-removal regression could pass on an unrelated busy refusal.
findings.gap: The kiln replacement-generation regression needs an assertion distinguishing pathname rebinding from unrelated lock contention; it is outside this tree. Stays with kiln's own tests: no kilnd VM scenario drives kiln's internal interleavings.

findings.summary: Stored evidence was not bound to the dispatched helper epoch and boot.
A departed Delete stranded a charged DELETING checkpoint.
Feature disablement stopped existing checkpoint maintenance.
Capture request keys from a prior boot never aged out.
Feature disablement rejected a retry already covered by durable idempotency.
Transient Inspect I/O permanently quarantined intact content.
An incomplete inventory blocked Create until restart.
Shutdown dropped the source hold before capture-worker absence.
Startup admission opened without accounting for all artifacts and operations.
Caller cancellation before C1 still created a charged checkpoint.
Feature-off settled history bypassed a failed-session barrier.
Pruning the last row left feature-off paths querying checkpoint storage.
Startup removed a source before its interrupted capture worker.
Last-row pruning could clear a failed-session barrier without inventory.
D1 dropped an interrupted capture source hold before ABSENT.
A long grace bypassed the shutdown drain limit.
Restart after last-row pruning forgot the inventory obligation.
Feature-off sandbox Delete while blocked lacked a direct coverage control.
An unsealed QUARANTINED store row is outside the source-hold predicate.
findings.reason: Production quarantines only sealed READY rows; any future unsealed quarantine path must extend the source-hold rule.

findings.summary: A retained unsealed removal can hold its source until operator repair.
findings.reason: Fail-closed source retention is required until authoritative ABSENT evidence.

findings.summary: Feature-off restart forgot a rowless blocked barrier.
Crash before marker commit lost an already observed inventory obligation.
An unsupported backend cleared a rowless marker without inventory.
Restart admitted Create beside a failed capture with retained artifacts.
The checkpoint retry could not clear its own shared admission latch after successful removal.
A capture failure after a pass snapshot survived a stale clear.
A sealed quarantined row explains an inventory ID without validating replacement content.
findings.reason: A sealed quarantine retains S and refuses forks; tracked bindings remain checked and Delete requires exact absence.

findings.summary: Release wakes can re-drive another retained row before its individual backoff.
findings.reason: Allocation is blocked and finite release wakes bound the extra work; a retained verdict does not itself wake the retry.
findings.gap: No direct pacing regression pins the documented bound or distinguishes global release wakes from a per-row one-minute promise.

findings.summary: Orderly VM shutdown did not exercise blocked restart with retained real-helper artifacts.
A tracked capture failure after a clean clear did not globally re-arm allocation.
findings.reason: The invariant ruling permits runtime overlap while cleanup is owned and charge retained; stale in-flight pass clears and ownership loss still block.

findings.summary: A failed failure-record write lost capture cleanup tracking and left admission open.
Supervisor panic lacked an exit guard and could lose cleanup ownership.
Simultaneous supervisor exits would need atomic ownership checks in a multi-thread embedding.
Restart discarded final restore outcomes and stranded sandbox reservations.
Fork admission allocated after the global barrier was raised.
Caller Exec argv impersonated a privileged checkpoint worker.
Durable fork failures lost their typed reason.
Restore-proven corruption left the checkpoint READY.
Checkpoint ABSENT discarded an orphan fork settlement handle.
Dead-epoch startup retained an untyped keyed fork failure.
An orphan path released a reservation while its recorded backend still ran.
Settlement write failures were treated as a clean pass.
Worker argv parser accepted command lines kiln refuses.
Startup published a recorded fork that settlement deliberately kept blocked.
Fork publication compensation stored an untyped keyed failure.
Worker parser differed from kiln clap grammar at signed-zero, empty and non-UTF-8 edges.
Required capture options and CREATING-fork retention lacked direct mutation guards.
Canceled fork requests still crossed durable admission.
Small list pages scanned all retained history.
CLI checkpoint listing failed under valid page caps below 100.
A reconnect let checkpoint Create bypass its feature check.
New-work storage probe failures also blocked Delete and cleanup.
Health omitted an accounting-quarantined checkpoint charge.
Run cleanup could report nothing sent after Exec reached the daemon.

A restore that found the artifact corrupt after allocating (kiln checks object digests in the shim) left the checkpoint READY instead of QUARANTINED, so later forks were admitted and failed the same way.
